FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (Fourth Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized 
by the Secondary Cells and Batteries Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electrotechnical Division 
Council. 


This standard was first published in 1960 and subsequently revised three times. 


The first revision of this standard had been undertaken with a view to extend the scope to cover capacities up to 
1 000 Ah and to delete the details about the inner construction of cells. The opportunity had also been utilized to 
incorporate all the four amendments issued to the 1960 version of the standard. 


The second revision was brought out to modify the maximum overall dimensions and to include the requirements 
of endurance test, ampere-hour and watt-hour efficiency tests and test for voltages during discharge. The scope 
of the standard was widened by covering lead-lined wood as well as FRP containers and by extending the capacity 
range of cells up to 5 000 Ah. The batteries with monobloc construction were excluded. 


The third revision of this standard had been undertaken in 1991 to include some major amendments carried out 
in cell dimensions, test methods and test requirements. 


This fourth revision has been undertaken to incorporate the latest developments and includes Parameters for 
Normal Discharge Performance (NDP) Cells, High Discharge Performance (HDP) Cells as well as Lead-acid 
cells with tubular positive plates and pasted negative plates housed in transparent SAN containers (TBS cells) 
and also some new tests requirements, like water loss test, test of suitability of floating battery operation, short 
circuit current and internal resistance test. 


The tests for performance specified in this standard are to be carried out in prevalent ambient conditions. The 
results of such tests should be corrected to the standard atmospheric conditions according to the correction 
factors specified. 


Only cell interchangeability is feasible in the type of cells and batteries covered by this standard as opposed to 
the plate interchangeability achieved in batteries using plante positive plates. Further, size-to-size exchange of 
batteries using tubular plates with those using plante plates also is not possible since the cells with tubular plate 
construction are smaller in size. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 
‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised) . The number of significant places retained in the rounded off 
value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 1651 : 2013 


Indian Standard 


STATIONARY CELLS AND BATTERIES, LEAD-ACID 
TYPE ( WITH TUBULAR POSITIVE

( Fourth Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard specifies rated Ah capacities, overall 
dimensions, performance requirements and tests for 
stationary lead-acid cells and batteries using tubular 
positive plates. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards listed in Annex A contain provisions 
which, through reference in this text, constitute 
provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, 
the editions indicated were valid. All standards are 
subject to revision, and parties to agreements based on 
this standard are encouraged to investigate the 
possibility of applying the most recent editions of the 
standards listed in Annex A. 


3 TERMINOLOGY 


For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given 
in IS 1885 (Part 8) and the following shall apply. 


3.1 Fully-Charged Condition — The cell shall be 
considered as fully charged when the specific gravity 
readings and the voltage of the cell, at a specific 
temperature remains constant over three consecutive 
hourly readings; the charging rate during the period 
being maintained constant. 


3.2 Normal Discharge Performance (NDP) Cells — 
Lead acid cells with tubular positive plates and pasted 
negative plates meeting the discharge performance 
given in Table 6. 


3.3 High Discharge Performance (HDP) Cells — 
Specially designed cells with tubular positive plates 
and pasted negative plates. These cells shall meet the 
discharge characteristics as given in Table 7. 


3.4 TBS Cells — Lead acid cells with tubular positive 
plates and pasted negative plates housed in transparent 
SAN containers. 


3.5 Type Tests — Tests carried out to prove 
conformity with the requirements of this standard. 
These are intended to prove the general quality and 
design of a given type of battery. 


3.6 Acceptance Tests — Tests carried out on samples 
selected from a lot for the purpose of verifying the 
acceptability of the lot. 


3.6.1 Lot — All batteries of the same type, design 
and rating, manufactured by the same factory during 
the same period, using the same process and materials, 
offered for inspection at a time shall constitute a lot. 


3.7 Routine Tests — Tests carried out on every 
battery. 
4 RATING AND DESIGNATION 


4.1 Ampere-Hour Rating 
4.1.1 For NDP and HDP Cells 


The rating assigned to the cell shall be the capacity 
expressed in ampere-hours (after correction to 27°C) 
stated by the manufacturer to be obtainable when the 
cell is discharged at the 10 h rate (C.o) to a final voltage 
of 1.85 volts. 


4.1.2 For TBS Cells 


The rating assigned to the cell shall be the capacity 
expressed in ampere-hours (after correction to 27°C) 
stated by the manufacturer to be obtainable when the 
cell is discharged at the 10 h rate (C;) to a final voltage 
of 1.80 V. 


4.2 Designation 
4.2.1 For NDP and HDP Cells 


The cell shall be designated by symbols given below, 
arranged in the following sequence: 


( Type of (Ah Rating ( Type of 
Positive Plate ) of Cell) Container ) 
(see 4.2.1.1) (see 4.2.1.2) (see 4.2.1.3) 
NOTES 


1 The plates are not replaced in this type of construction, 
therefore, this designation does not include the number of 
positive plates. 

2 The designation of partially plated cells is not being 
standardized because partial plating of cells in this type of 
construction is not done. 


IS 1651 : 2013 


4.2.1.1 The positive plates being of tubular type shall 
be designated by the letter ‘T’. 


4.2.1.2 The capacity rating shall be indicated by a 
number equal to the capacity in Ah. 


4.2.1.3 The material of container shall be designated 
by any one of the following letters as the case may be: 
H — for hard-rubber, 
P — for plastics, 
F — for fibre reinforced plastics (FRP), and 
S — for SAN. 
Example: T 400 H HDP — designates a high discharge 


performance cell having tubular positive plates and a 
capacity of 400 Ah at 10 h rate in hard-rubber container. 


4.2.2 For TBS cells, the cells shall be designated as 
‘A’ TBS ‘B’. In this nomenclature, the term ‘A’ shall 
be a numeral indicating the number of positive plate 
in the cell and ‘B’ is another numeral describing the 
rated capacity of the cell as explained in 4.1.2 . 


5 MATERIALS 


5.1 Containers 


The containers shall be made of hard rubber, plastics 
or fibre reinforced plastics (FRP) for NDP and HDP 
cells. 


For TBS cells, the container shall be made of 
transparent SAN polymer. 


5.1.1 Hard rubber, fibre-reinforced plastic (FRP) 
containers and transparent SAN containers shall 
conform to IS 1146. 


5.2 Electrolyte 


The sulphuric acid and water used for the preparation 
and maintenance of electrolyte shall conform to IS 266 
and IS 1069, respectively. 


5.3 Sealing Compound 


Sealing compound, if bitumen based, shall conform to 
IS 3116. 


5.4 Separators 


The separators used shall be synthetic and shall 
conform to IS 6071. 


6 CONSTRUCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS 


6.1 Cell Lids 


Cell lids shall be either drop on type together with suitable 
rubber or plastics gasket or of the deep sealing type 
suitable for use with bituminous or a suitable sealing 
compound, with close-fitting terminal posts and with vent- 


holes suitable for accommodating the venting device. 


NOTE — Other methods of sealing when used shall not 
contaminate the electrolyte when these come in contact. A 
suitable method for determining such requirements is under 
consideration and shall be included at a later date. 


6.2 Venting Device 
6.2.1 For NDP and HPD Cell 


The venting device shall be of anti-splash type with 
more than one exit hole and shall allow the gases to 
escape freely but shall effectively prevent acid particles 
or spray from coming out. For capacities 120 Ah and 
above, there shall be two vent holes, one serving as a 
guide for the acid-level and the other to permit drawing 
of electrolyte samples, servicing, checking of specific 
gravity, etc. 


6.2.2 For TBS Cells 


The containers being transparent, these cells do not 
require any extra electrolyte level indicator, hence 
one venting hole on the lid would suffice. However, 
depending on the size of the cell more than one venting 
hole may also be provided. 


6.3 Electrolyte Level Indicator 
6.3.1 For NDP and HDP Cells 


A suitable electrolyte level indicator indicating lower 
and upper limits shall be fitted to facilitate checking 
of electrolyte level in opaque containers. The materials 
used shall be acid proof and shall not deteriorate during 
service. 


6.3.2 For TBS Cells 


The containers being transparent, these cells do not 
require any extra electrolyte level indicator. The 
container, however, shall be clearly and indelibly 
marked with the requisite maximum and minimum 
operating electrolyte levels. 


6.4 Terminal Posts 


Positive and negative terminal posts shall be clearly 
and unmistakably identifiable. 


6.5 Connectors 


The manufacturer’s identification shall be indicated on 
the connectors. Where it is not possible to bolt the cell 
terminals directly to assemble a battery, separate lead, 
copper or aluminium connectors of suitable size shall 
be provided to enable connection of the cells. In some 
cases, it may be necessary to connect individual cells 
in parallel. In such cases the connectors shall be 
suitably designed. The cross-section area of the 
connectors are to be sufficient to have a maximum 
current density of 2.5 A/mm? for lead connectors and 


15 A/mm? for copper connectors when the discharge 
current of 1 min rate is considered. In case copper 
connector or aluminium connectors, when used for 
discharge at a very high rates are not plastic 
encapsulated, should be suitably coated with lead to 
withstand corrosion due to sulphuric acid. In such 
cases, the thickness of lead-coating of connectors 
should be not less than 0.025 mm and the lead coating 
thickness shall be measured in accordance with 
Appendix F of IS 6848. 


6.6 Nuts and Bolts 


The material for bolts and nuts shall be brass/mild steel/ 
SS. Bolts and nuts, for connecting the cells, shall be 
effectively lead-coated to prevent corrosion from 
sulphuric acid. The fasteners when used in bolt-on type 
terminal shall pereferably have a plastic head for 
insulation purpose with an access point to enable 
voltage measurement.

8 MARKING AND PACKING 


8.1 Marking 


The following information shall be indelibly and 
durably marked on the outside of the cell: 


a) Indicating the source of manufacture, 
b) Ah capacity at 10 h rate, 


c) Upper and lower electrolyte level in case of 
transparent containers, 


d) Year of manufacture, and 
e) Country of origin. 


8.1.1 BIS Certification Marking 
The cells may also be marked with the Standard Mark. 


8.1.1.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by 
the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 
1986 and the rules and regulations made thereunder. 
The details of conditions under which a licence for the 
use of the Standard Mark may be granted to 
manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the 
Bureau of Indian Standards. 


8.2 Packing 


The cells shall be suitably packed so as to avoid any 
loss or damage during transit.

10 CONDITIONS OF SUPPLY 


10.1 To facilitate procurement of correct type of 
stationary cells, it is recommended that the user should 
furnish information regarding his requirements given 
in Annex B at the time of enquiry or order. Similarly, 
the manufacturer should furnish the information given 
in Annex C. 


10.2 Other conditions of supply shall be subject to 
agreement between the purchaser and the supplier. 


11 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS FOR TESTS 


11.1 Temperature for Testing 


Unless it becomes unavoidable, test discharge should 
not be taken when the temperature of the electrolyte 
exceeds 35°C. 


11.2 Test Equipment 
11.2.1 Voltmeter 


The voltmeter used for tests shall be of an accuracy 
class not inferior to 0.5 in accordance with IS 1248. 
The resistance of the volt-meter used shall be at least 
1 000 ohms per volt (see IS 1248). The range of the 
voltmeter used shall be such that the magnitude of the 
voltage to be measured falls in the last third part of the 
scale. 


11.2.2 Ammeter 


The ammeter used for tests shall have an accuracy class 
not inferior to 1.0 (see IS 1248). The range of ammeter 
used shall be such that the magnitude of the current to 
be measured falls in the last third part of the scale. 


11.2.3 Thermometer 


A thermometer with an appropriate scale shall be used 
for measuring temperature and one division of the 
graduated scale shall represent at the most 1°C. 

NOTE — The voltmeter, the ammeter and the thermometer of 


digital read-out type of similar accuracy also can be used. Data 
loggers may be used during charge/discharge activity. 


11.2.4 Hydrometer 


The specific gravity of the electrolyte shall be measured 
by a hydrometer provided with a graduated scale, one 
division of which shall represent at the most 0.005 unit 
of specific gravity. 
The accuracy of calibration shall be not less than 
0.005 unit of specific gravity. 
NOTE — In view of the compact construction of this type of 
cells, it may not be possible to measure the specific gravity 


directly by floating hydrometer. Hence, the use of syringe type 
of hydrometer will generally have to be resorted to. 


11.3 First Charge 


The cell, if received in dry and uncharged condition 
shall be filled with the electrolyte and shall be first 
charged in accordance with the manufacturer’s 
instructions. 


11.4 Specific Gravity of Electrolyte 
11.4.1 For NDP and HDP Cells 


The standard specific gravity of a fully charged cell 
shall be adjusted to 1.200 + 0.005 corrected at 27°C 
in accordance with 11.4 of IS 8320. 


11.4.2 For TBS Cells 


The standard specific gravity of a fully charged cell 
shall be adjusted to 1.240 + 0.005 corrected at 27°C in 
accordance with 11.4 of IS 8320. 


11.5 Observation 


11.5.1 While charging the cell, the voltmeter, 
hydrometer and thermometer readings shall be recorded 
at suitable intervals. 


11.5.2 During the discharge at 10 h rate the voltmeter 
readings shall be recorded every hour for the first 8 h 
and every 15 min thereafter up to the end voltage. 


11.5.3 The hydrometer and thermometer readings at 
hourly intervals and at the end of the discharge shall be 
recorded only on the pilot cell(s). 


11.5.4 The first and the last reading of hydro meter 
and thermometer shall be made on all the cells. 


11.6 Temperature Factors of Capacity 


11.6.1 The correction of the capacity to 27°C shall be 
carried out in accordance with 11.6.2. The values for 
correction factors shall be chosen from Table 3. 


11.6.2 The capacity shall be corrected to 27°C by the 
following formula: 


C,x Rx (27-1)

11.7 Water shall be added, if required to correct the 
electrolyte level during a test after a full charge. 
However, after such water addition, cells should be 
given a freshening charge for suitable duration so that 
thorough mixing with electrolyte is facilitated. 


12 TESTS 


12.1 Classification of Tests 
12.1.1 Type Tests for NDP and HDP Cells 


The following shall constitute type test and shall be 
carried out in the given sequence: 


a) Verification of constructional requirements 
(see 12.2), 


b) Verification of marking (see 12.3), 
c) Verification of dimensions (see 12.4), 


d) Test for capacity (see 12.5) — Test for voltage 
during discharge (see 12.10), 


e) Ampere-hour and watt-hour efficiency tests 
(see 12.9), 


f) Test for loss of capacity on storage (see 12.7), 
g) Endurance test (see 12.8), and 
h) Water loss test (see 12.11). 


IS 1651 : 2013 


12.1.2 Type Tests for TBS Cells 


a) Verification of constructional requirements 
(see 12.2), 


b) Verification of marking (see 12.3), 

c) Verification of dimensions (see 12.4), 

d) Test for capacity (see 12.5) — Test for voltage 
during discharge (see 12.10), 

e) Ampere-hour and watt-hour efficiency tests 
(see 12.9), 

f) Test for loss of capacity on storage (see 12.7), 

g) Endurance test (see 12.8), 

h) Test for suitability of floating battery operation 
(see 12.12), 

j) Short circuit current and internal resistance 
test (see 12.13), and 

k) Water loss test (see 12.11). 


12.1.3 For conducting type tests for NDP and HDP 
cells, formed positive plates along with components 
for the six cells shall be chosen at random. 


The selected cells shall undergo the different type tests 
as per the schedule given in Table 4. 


12.1.4 For conducting type tests for TBS cells, formed 
positive plates along with components for the eight cells 
shall be chosen at random. 


The selected cells shall undergo the different type tests 
as per the schedule given in Table 5. 


12.1.5 If any of the samples fails in the relevant type 
test, testing authority may call for fresh samples not 
exceeding twice the original number and subject them 
again to all tests or test in which the failure has occurred 
as agreed to between the manufacturer and the buyer. 
If there is any failure in any of the retest, the type shall 
be considered as not having passed the requirements 
of this standard. 


12.1.6 Acceptance Tests 
The following shall constitute the acceptance tests: 


a) Marking and packing, 

b) Verification of dimensions, 

c) Test for capacity, and 

d) ‘Test for voltages during discharge. 
12.1.6.1 Acceptance tests shall, normally, be carried 
out, at the discretion of the purchaser. The date and 


place of testing shall be subject to agreement between 
the purchaser and the supplier. 


12.1.6.2 Sampling scheme and criteria for acceptance 


The sampling scheme and criteria for acceptance for 
cells up to and including 600 Ah capacity shall be in

12.2 Verification of Constructional Requirements 


The cells shall meet the requirements specified in 6. 


12.3 Verification of Marking and Packing 


The marking on the cells and their packing shall be in 
accordance with the requirement of 8. 


12.4 Verification of Dimensions 


The overall dimensions of cells of standard capacities 
shall conform to the requirements given in Tables 1 
and 2 as the case may be. 


12.5 Test for Capacity 


12.5.1 After standing on open circuit for not less than 
12 hand not more than 24 h, from the completion of a 
full charge, the cell shall be discharged through a 
suitable variable resistance at a constant current of 
I=0.1 Cio A. The discharge shall be stopped when the 
closed-circuit voltage across the cell falls to 1.85 V 
for NDP and HDP cells and 1.80 V for TBS cells. If 
however, a test discharge cannot be conducted within 
the specified rest period due to any exigencies, a 


freshening charge may be given to the cell/battery at 
the finishing rate of charge recommended by the 
manufacturer for a period of 1 h after every 24 h or 
part thereof, of extended rest period. The capacity test, 
however, can be started after a minimum period of 2 h 
elapsing after this freshening charge. 


12.5.2 The time in hours elapsing between the 
beginning and the end of discharge shall be taken as 
the period of discharge. 


12.5.3 The average temperature (t°C) of the electrolyte 
during discharge shall be the average of the 
temperatures of the electrolyte noted at hourly intervals. 


12.5.4 Unless otherwise agreed, capacity test as 
described above, and conducted immediately after the 
first charge of the cell is normally to be treated as the 
test discharge for the purpose of acceptance of the cell. 
On the first discharge the cell shall give not less than 
85 percent of the rated capacity and the rated capacity 
shall be reached within specified number of charge/ 
discharge cycles given by the supplier subject to 
maximum of 10 discharges subsequent to the initial 
charge. Once the rated capacity has been met on any 
discharge/further discharge cycles for capacity shall not 
be continued. 


12.5.5 For the purpose of acceptance test, the test for 


capacity may, by agreement between the purchaser and 
the supplier, be carried out at a rate other than the 10 h 
rate. In such cases, the 5 h rate is recommended. 
Capacities at various rates of discharge and 
corresponding final voltages are given in Table 6 for 
NDP cells, Table 7 for HDP cells and Table 8 for TBS 
cells. For the purpose of acceptance, the capacity test 
shall be carried out at one rate only. 


12.5.6 Correction for the variation of capacity with 
temperature shall be made in accordance with 11.5. 
The measured temperature shall be as specified 
in 12.5.3. 


12.5.7 Requirement 


12.5.7.1 The actual capacity shall not be less than the 
rated capacity and not more than 120 percent of the rated 
capacity when the test is carried out at the 10 h rate for 
NDP type cells. For HDP and TBS type cells, the actual

12.5.7.2 For the acceptance test when the test is carried

shall be not less than the corresponding rated capacity. 


12.6 Alternative Rates of Test Discharges 


12.6.1 An alternative test for capacity may, by 
agreement between the purchaser and the manufacturer, 
be conducted for High Discharge Performance (HDP) 
cells at the rates given in Table 7. 


12.6.2 Correction for the variation of capacity with 
temperature shall be in accordance with 11.6. The 
measured temperature shall be as specified in 12.5.3. 


12.6.3 Requirement for HDP Cells 


The actual capacity shall not be less than the rated 
capacity and not more than 130 percent of the rated 
capacity when the test is carried out at the 10 h rate. 


12.6.4 For the acceptance test of HDP cells, when the 
test is carried out at a rate other than the 10 h rate the 
actual capacity shall be not less than the corresponding 
rated capacity. 


12.7 Loss of Capacity on Storage 


12.7.1 This test shall be carried out on the one or two 
cells which have successfully passed the capacity test 
in accordance with 12.5. 


12.7.2 The cell shall be fully recharged at the current 
specified by the manufacturer and shall then be 
submitted to two consecutive capacity tests in 
accordance with 12.5, the value of the initial capacity 
C being calculated as the mean of the two results 
thus obtained. 


12.7.3 After a complete recharge and the cleaning of

at a temperature of 27 + 2°C. 


12.7.4 After the storage for 28 days, the cell shall be 
discharged in accordance with 12.5. The value of 
capacity measured after storage is denoted by C’.

12.7.6 Requirement 


The loss in capacity thus measured shall not exceed 
10 percent. 


12.8 Endurance Test 


12.8.1 The test shall be conducted on cells which have 
not been subjected to any other tests subsequent to 
initial charge as per the manufacturer’s instructions. 


12.8.2 The test shall be conducted on a complete cell. 


12.8.2.1 For HDP cells, the cell shall be charged 
continuously at a current 7 = 0.1 x C, A for total period 
of 2 000 h as given below: 


a) 2 Cycles of 300 h charging followed by test 
discharge, 

b) 3 Cycles of 200 h charging followed by test 
discharge, and 

c) 8 Cycles of 100 h charging followed by test 
discharge. 


12.8.2.2 For NDP cells, the cell shall be charged 
continuously at a current 7 = 0.1 x C,, A for total period 
of 1 500 h as given below: 


a) 1 Cycle of 300 h charging followed by test 
discharge, 

b) 2 Cycles of 200 h charging followed by test 
discharge, and 

c) 8 Cycles of 100 h charging followed by test 
discharge. 


12.8.2.3 For TBS cells, the cells shall be charged 
continuously at a current J = 0.1 x Cj) A for a period 
of 2 500 h as given below: 


a) 2 Cycles of 300 h charging followed by test 
discharge, 

b) 3 Cycles of 200 h charging followed by test 
discharge, and 


c) 13 Cycles of 100 h charging followed by test 
discharge. 


12.8.2.4 Throughout these periods of charge the cell 


shall be immersed in a tank of water the temperature 
of which shall be maintained at 40 + 3°C. The cell 
shall be so immersed that the top of cell is 25 mm above 
the water level in the tank. If several cells are placed in 
the same tank, a distance of 25 mm shall be maintained 
between them. This distance between a cell and the 
side of the tank shall be at least 25 mm. 


12.8.3 At the end of each period of charging (a), (b) 
and (c ) as specified in 12.8.2.1 and 12.8.2.2 and at the 
end of each unit of over charge as given in 12.8.2.3 the 
cell shall be subjected to a test discharge (C,,) to an 
end voltage of 1.85 V for NDP and HDP cells and 1.80 
V for TBS cells. This discharge shall be conducted 
without undue delay and without removing the cell from 
the water bath and shall be made within 2 h of 
termination of the charging current (see 12.8.2). 


If for any reason, the time between the termination of 
charging (see 12.8.2) and the test discharge exceeds 
2 h, the cell in the water bath may, at the option of the 
manufacturer, be kept on a, ‘trickle charge’ not 
exceeding J = 0.01 x C,, A until the time of test 
discharge. 


12.8.3.1 When the test discharge is complete, the cell 
shall be immediately subjected to the next period of 
continuous charge without any recharging. 


12.8.4 Requirement 


The obtained C,, capacity should be more than 
80 percent of its rated capacity at the end of the entire 
over charge period of 1 500 h, 2 000 h and 2 500 h for 
NDP, HDP and TBS, respectively. 


12.9 Ampere-Hour and Watt-Hour Efficiency Tests 
12.9.1 Ampere-Hour Efficiency 


A fully charged cell shall be discharged at J = 0.1 
x Cio A to an end voltage of 1.85 V for NDP and HDP 
cells and 1.80 V for TBS cells, careful calculations 
being made of the exact number of ampere-hours 
delivered. On recharge the same number of ampere- 
hours are put back at the same current. A second 
discharge shall then be made to the same cut-off voltage 
as before. The efficiency of the cell is then calculated 
as the ratio of the ampere-hour delivered during the 
second discharge to the ampere-hour put in on the 
charge. 


12.9.1.1 Requirement 


The ampere-hour efficiency when calculated as 
described in 12.9.1 shall be not less than 92 percent. 


12.9.2 Watt-Hour Efficiency 


The watt-hour efficiency shall be calculated by 
multiplying the ampere-hour efficiency by the ratio 
average discharge and recharge voltage. The values of 


discharge and recharge voltages shall be calculated 
from the log sheets for ampere-hour efficiency test. The 
average voltage shall be calculated from the ‘hourly’ 
readings of the discharge voltage but including the 
voltage immediately after start of discharge and last 
reading. 


Similarly for calculating the average voltage during 
recharge the only ‘hourly voltage readings (including 
the voltage immediately after starting the charge and 
the last reading before charge is terminated) shall be 
taken. 


12.9.2.1 Requirement 


The watt-hour efficiency when calculated as described 
in 12.9.2 shall be not less than 80 percent. 


12.10 Test for Voltage During Discharge 


The cell need not be discharged specially for this test. 
For the purposes of this test the voltages shall be 
obtained from the log sheets for capacity test (see 12.5) 
in which the cell meets the rated capacity. 


12.10.1 Requirement 


The closed circuit voltage of cell shall not be below 
the values given in col 2 below:

12.11 Water Loss Test 


This test shall be carried out on two cells which have 
qualified the capacity test according to 12.5. After 
fully charging the cell it should be cleaned and dried. 
It should be weighed immediately but not exceeding 
1 h after drying with an accuracy of 0.05 percent or 
maximum least count of 10 g for the balance used. 
Then all vent-cum-filling plugs should be closed 
tightly and connected to constant voltage charger 
keeping the voltage 2.4 + 0.05 volt/cell for 21 days 
in water bath at a temperature of 50 + 2°C . Thereafter 
the cell is removed from circuit, dried and weighed 
accurately. 


12.11.1 Requirement 


The water loss shall not exceed 0.8 g/Ah/cell of the 
obtained capacity for NDP and HDP cells and 
0.5g/Ah/cell for TBS cells. 


IS 1651 : 2013 


12.12 Test of Suitability of Floating Battery 
Operation 


The test shall be carried out on a group of two cells 
which have qualified the capacity discharge test 
according to 12.5. 


The cells shall be kept at an ambient as close as 
practically possible to the reference temperature of 
27°C and the upper surface of the lid shall be kept 
clean and dry throughout the duration of the test. 


The cells shall be subjected to a constant float voltage 
as per the manufacturer’s recommendation during the 
test. The initial voltage of the cells across the terminals 
shall be measured and recorded. 


After intervals of three months the float voltage, 
specific gravity and the electrolyte level of each cell 
shall be measured and recorded. After six months of 
continuous floating operation, the cells shall be 
subjected to a capacity discharge according to 12.5. 


12.12.1 Requirement 


Cells tested as per the above procedure shall meet the 
following requirements: 


a) The electrolyte densities shall remain within 
the specified tolerance limits as recommended 
by the manufacturer; 

b) The individual cell voltages shall remain 
within the specified tolerance limits as 
recommended by the manufacturer; and 

c) After a period of six months, the obtained 
capacity on discharge according to 12.5 shall 
at least be equal to the rated capacity of the 
cell. 


12.13 Short Circuit Current and Internal 
Resistance Test 


The test shall be conducted on minimum number of 
two cells which have qualified the capacity test 
according to 12.5. 


After fully charging the cells as per the manufacturer’s 
recommendation, the cells shall be kept in ambient 
temperature and the discharge characteristics, U =f (D) 
of the cells is then established by finding out two of its 
points by the following way: 


a) First Point (U, I,)— The cells are discharged 
at a current J, = 4/,)...... 61,, A. After 20 s of 
such discharge the voltage and the current are 
measured and these values give the first point 
(U,, 1). 

The discharge shall be interrupted after 25 s 
maximum and the cells shall be kept on open 


IS 1651 : 2013 


circuit, without recharging, for 2 to 5 min 
before the second point is determined. 
Second Point (U, I,) — The cells are then 
discharged at a current of J, = 20/,)........ 401, 
A. The voltage and current are measured 
after 5 s of onset of this discharge and form 
the second point (U,, L). 


b)

by linearly joining the two points (U,, /,) and 
(U, L) as in Fig.1. The line can be linearly 
extrapolated to U=0 V. The intercept indicates 
the short-circuit current Z The internal

gradient of the U =f (J) line.

Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods 
and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form 
without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of 
implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. 
Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 


‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards : Monthly Additions’. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: ETD 11 (6166).
